title: Understanding Territorial Behavior as a Key to Design of Formal Care Spaces for Children

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village bedrooms in Nicosia
findings.consequent: degree of mess and disorder by children
findings.mechanism: staff policy/expectation for tidiness overriding child's natural territorial marking behavior
findings.quote: all nine children’s bedrooms were clean and tidy.

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village bedrooms in Vienna
findings.consequent: degree of mess and disorder by children (personal belongings spread, beds made by children's effort)
findings.mechanism: staff awareness of mess as territorial marking and allowing child agency
findings.quote: in Vienna although all five children’s bedrooms were clean, mostly their personal belongings were spread all over the rooms

findings.antecedent: bedroom environment (support for self-presentation)
findings.mechanism: provision of means for self-expression and identity display
findings.quote: five of fourteen bedrooms... have high degree of self-presentation

findings.antecedent: bedroom environment (lack of support for self-presentation)
findings.mechanism: lack of means for self-expression and identity display
findings.quote: other six bedrooms... have low self-presentation

findings.antecedent: shared bedrooms in Nicosia SOS Children's Village
findings.mechanism: lack of intentional design for territorial demarcation
findings.quote: In 9 out of 14 bedrooms, which are located in Nicosia, there are no sign of shaping any proper identifiable and noticeable territory.

findings.antecedent: shared bedrooms in Vienna SOS Children's Village with symmetrical division, furniture placement, different wall colors, rugs, names/photos
findings.mechanism: intentional design and caregiver support for territoriality
findings.quote: in three from remained five children’s bedrooms, which are located in Vienna, there are some signs of symmetrical division

findings.antecedent: child age (above 10 years old) and bedroom type (private rooms with walls and doors) in Vienna
findings.mechanism: provision of private rooms for older children to meet privacy and space demands
findings.quote: The other two bedrooms are private rooms, for children above 10 years old who demand for more space and privacy

findings.antecedent: caregiver consideration of child's views in furniture arrangement
findings.mechanism: child involvement in shaping their environment
findings.quote: only in 6 out of 14 bedrooms... children’s points of views were considered in room’s rearrangement.

findings.antecedent: furniture additions in Nicosia bedrooms (not chosen by children)
findings.mechanism: lack of child agency in personalization
findings.quote: these additions such as a small desk, coach, arm chair, etc., did not help to better adjustment of children

findings.antecedent: shared bedrooms for three children with fewer occupants (extra furniture present)
findings.mechanism: lack of adaptation to actual occupancy
findings.quote: the extra furniture were not removed from the bedrooms to give more space to children.

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village location (Nicosia)
findings.consequent: provision of adequate furniture for each child
findings.mechanism: resource constraints leading to shared furniture
findings.quote: serious lack of furniture in 9 out of 14 children’s bedrooms which all were located in Nicosia.

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village location (Vienna)
findings.consequent: provision of adequate furniture for each child
findings.mechanism: better resource allocation
findings.quote: in the last three bedrooms and number of furniture was adequate for each individual who is accommodated in the bedrooms.

findings.antecedent: sharing main furniture
findings.mechanism: lack of individual ownership over shared items
findings.quote: children have to share main furniture so they display less personalization.

findings.antecedent: bedroom environment (support for child involvement in personalization)
findings.mechanism: child agency and self-expression
findings.quote: 5 out of 14 bedrooms, one in Nicosia and four in Vienna, were personalized mostly by children

findings.antecedent: bedroom environment (lack of support for child involvement in personalization)
findings.mechanism: lack of child agency and self-expression
findings.quote: 9 out of 14 bedrooms shows lack of children’s involvement in personalization or even personalization itself.

findings.antecedent: degree of personalization (low)
findings.consequent: child adjustment and attachment to bedrooms
findings.mechanism: personalization as a means to create a link with a place
findings.quote: due to the low degree of personalization, the level of adjustment and attachment to the bedrooms by children appeared to be not strong

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village location (Vienna vs Nicosia)
findings.mechanism: better design and caregiver support in Vienna
findings.quote: in case of Vienna the strength of this dimension was higher than the case of Nicosia

findings.antecedent: child age (girls above ten) and location (Vienna)
findings.mechanism: response to demand for privacy for older children
findings.quote: Girls above ten in Vienna who demand for more space and privacy occupy those two private rooms.

findings.antecedent: child age (above ten) and location (Nicosia)
findings.mechanism: lack of policy/resources for private rooms
findings.quote: this option (requesting for private room from certain age) is not available for children above ten years old in Nicosia.

findings.antecedent: shared bedrooms
findings.mechanism: lack of design for semi-private areas
findings.quote: none of the twelve shared bedrooms provide distinguishing physical boundaries by using physical space divisions

findings.antecedent: shared bedrooms
findings.mechanism: lack of design for visual barriers
findings.quote: other bedrooms are not planned and furnished in a way to provide even small barriers or boundaries to help children to have some visual privacy.

findings.antecedent: monitoring and supervision policy (high)
findings.consequent: child's ability to close bedroom doors
findings.mechanism: safety concerns overriding privacy needs
findings.quote: children are not allowed to close their bedroom’s doors due to the high level of monitoring and supervision

findings.antecedent: lack of physical barriers/room dividers and door closing restriction
findings.consequent: child's control over being intruded by roommates/peers
findings.mechanism: environmental constraints on privacy management
findings.quote: children do not have actually control over being intruded and bothered by their roommates and peers.

findings.antecedent: care setting (SOS Children's Village)
findings.mechanism: caregiver responsibility for child protection
findings.quote: all fourteen children’s bedrooms are supervised and monitored 24/7 by caregivers.

findings.antecedent: shared bedrooms in SOS Children's Village
findings.mechanism: lack of physical barriers and control over interactions
findings.quote: Summary of all indicators display significant low level of privacy in most of the cases (Figure 39).

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village location (Nicosia) and bed arrangement (in 3 rooms)
findings.mechanism: improper furniture arrangement
findings.quote: position of beds in three from fourteen rooms, which all located in Nicosia, cannot offer respectable personal space and distance

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village location (Nicosia) and bed arrangement (in 3 rooms)
findings.consequent: respectable personal space around beds (average, but problems with other furniture)
findings.mechanism: improper furniture arrangement
findings.quote: The other three bedrooms, which have average state of offering personal distance for beds, have problem with positions and arrangement of other furniture

findings.antecedent: bedroom type (private rooms) and bed arrangement (in 6 shared rooms)
findings.mechanism: adequate spacing and arrangement
findings.quote: Except the two private rooms, in the last six bedrooms, beds have respectable distance toward other beds and furniture.

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village location (Nicosia) and desk quantity (not enough)
findings.mechanism: insufficient furniture and improper arrangement
findings.quote: in five from fourteen rooms which all located in Nicosia, there are not enough desks available for each individual

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village location (Nicosia) and desk arrangement (in 2 rooms)
findings.consequent: respectable personal space around desks (average, but problematic position)
findings.mechanism: improper furniture arrangement
findings.quote: in the other two which have average state of offering personal distance, although there are enough desks due to the number of children in the rooms however the problem is the position of desks which are near to gather or to other furniture like closet or bed.

findings.antecedent: bedroom type (private rooms) and desk arrangement (in 5 shared rooms)
findings.mechanism: adequate spacing and arrangement
findings.quote: Except the two private rooms, the last five bedrooms offer respectable distance from other desks and furniture.

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village location (Nicosia) and closet quantity (only one fixed shared closet)
findings.mechanism: insufficient furniture and shared resources
findings.quote: position of closet in nine from fourteen rooms, which all are located in Nicosia, cannot offer respectable personal space, privacy and distance

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village location (Vienna) and closet quantity (individual closets)
findings.mechanism: provision of individual closets
findings.quote: In the other five bedrooms, position of closets can offer respectable state of personal distance for each individual during dressing.

findings.antecedent: bedroom type (private rooms)
findings.mechanism: inherent privacy of private rooms
findings.quote: only in two privet bedrooms, respectable privacy is available for children during dressing.

findings.antecedent: closet provision (number not matched to children)
findings.mechanism: insufficient furniture provision
findings.quote: personal distance among children’s closet in most of the cases is highly sited in low level of consideration since the number of closets are not measured due to the number of children.

findings.antecedent: furniture provision and arrangement (for desks and beds)
findings.consequent: personal distance around desks and beds
findings.mechanism: better furniture provision and arrangement for these items
findings.quote: this situation is better for children desks and beds (Figure 40).

findings.antecedent: SOS Children's Village location (Vienna vs Nicosia)
findings.mechanism: better furniture provision and arrangement in Vienna
findings.quote: in case of Vienna the strength of this dimension was higher than the case of Nicosia.
